title: Nodes That Cannot Loop Forever
statement:
A directed graph has n nodes numbered 0 to n − 1. graph[i] lists the nodes that node i has an edge to. A node with no outgoing edges is a dead end.

Call a node safe if every walk that starts there, whatever edges it picks, reaches a dead end after finitely many steps. In other words, no walk from it can go on forever. Return all safe nodes in increasing order.

examples.why: Node 2 can step to the dead end 3, but it can also go back to 0 and circle 0 → 1 → 2 forever. One escape route is not enough.
No cycles at all, so every walk ends at node 3.
Node 0 has an edge to itself, so it can loop forever, and so can node 1 by stepping into 0.

constraints: graph[i] is sorted with no repeats; self-edges are allowed
hints: A node is unsafe exactly when some walk from it can reach a cycle. How do you detect cycles with DFS?
Colour nodes: unvisited, on the current DFS path, finished-and-safe. Meeting a node on the current path means a cycle; anything that can reach it is unsafe too.
Or work backwards: dead ends are safe. Reverse every edge; a node becomes safe once all of its outgoing edges lead to safe nodes. That is Kahn's topological sort on the reversed graph.

explain.intuition:
Forever means a cycle: a finite graph only allows an endless walk if the walk eventually goes around a cycle. So a node is safe exactly when nothing reachable from it lies on a cycle.

The backward view is the cleanest. Dead ends are safe. A node whose every edge points to a safe node is safe as well. Keep, for each node, how many of its outgoing edges still lead to not-yet-proven nodes. Start a queue with the dead ends; when a node is proven safe, walk its incoming edges and decrement those counters. Nodes that reach 0 are safe. Whatever never reaches 0 can reach a cycle. It is Kahn's algorithm on the reversed graph, the same idea a bundler uses to find which modules are free of circular imports.
steps: Build the reversed graph: for every edge i → j, record i in rev[j]. Let out[i] = graph[i].length.
Put every node with out[i] = 0 in a queue and mark it safe.
Pop a node j. For each i in rev[j], decrement out[i]; if it hits 0, mark i safe and push it.
Return all marked nodes in increasing order.
pitfalls: Calling a node safe because one path from it reaches a dead end. Every path must, as in the first example.
In the DFS version, marking a node as unsafe only when it is on a cycle. Nodes that merely lead into a cycle are unsafe too.
Forgetting self-edges. A node with an edge to itself is a cycle of length 1.

solutions.title: DFS with three colours
solutions.idea: Grey marks nodes on the current path, black marks proven safe nodes. Reaching a grey node means a cycle, and everything still grey stays unsafe.

solutions.title: Peel from the dead ends (reverse Kahn)
solutions.idea: Dead ends are safe; a node becomes safe once every outgoing edge points to a safe node. Propagate along reversed edges.

followups: Edges are added one at a time and you must report the number of safe nodes after each addition. What can only ever change in one direction?
Return one cycle that makes node 0 unsafe, or an empty list if it is safe.
